2102065567318638730.headline: Crew overwhelmingly votes yes, boarding the Alt. Enterprise-D

reasons.yes: Most saw joining a legendary crew on a maiden voyage as an easy, obvious call not worth debating.
reasons.no: The few dissenters worried about being an expendable background character on a ship full of leads.

2102065567318638730.wildcards: Recurring jokes about red-shirt mortality odds, and a persistent minority campaign to smuggle a beloved cookie along for the ride.

2102790343305626057.headline: Fleet overwhelmingly chose Sheppard's jumper run into the bay

reasons.sheppard: Crew favored the jumper as a reliable fallback with a built-in exit, letting them scout the hangar and bridge while keeping a ship on hand for a fast getaway.
reasons.scotty: Backers trusted Scotty's transporter as the simplest, fastest way aboard and preferred his track record over a risky trek through the ship.
reasons.garak: Supporters liked the hull-breach route for its surprise value and the chance to immediately learn what crippled the freighter.
reasons.mckay: A small contingent argued the mission wasn't worth the risk and preferred scanning, remote access, or flagging it for another ship entirely.

2102790343305626057.wildcards: Several officers floated hybrid plans pairing the jumper with Scotty on standby for emergency extraction, and more than one voice cited McKay's caution just to overrule it for the sake of a good story.

2103152730714063183.headline: Fleet backs Row D, O'Neill-Jackson-McKay-Rommie squad wins narrow plurality

reasons.D: Voters liked a no-medic-needed lineup with strong translation, tech repair, and vacuum survival covered without redundant piloting.
reasons.A: Voters wanted Data's vacuum tolerance and analytical strength paired with medical coverage from Frasier for maximum self-sufficiency.
reasons.C: Voters favored O'Neill and Carter's chemistry plus Odo and Garak for infiltration, shapeshifting access, and reading potential traps.
reasons.B: Voters prioritized heavy security and McCoy's medical expertise in case the mission turned into a rescue or firefight.

2103152730714063183.wildcards: Recurring gags included wanting a hybrid team that didn't exist as an option, jokes about defaulting to 'C' on multiple-choice instinct, and speculation about odd-couple pairings like Bones and Teal'c.

2103515118818697677.headline: O'Neill's suit-up gambit won decisively, with McKay's hard line a distant second.

reasons.oneill: Fans prized keeping the retreat route open, wary that hangar doors forced shut might never reopen if things went bad.
reasons.mckay: Backers judged the jumper's small power drain an acceptable, recoverable cost for a properly sealed and pressurized bay.
reasons.rommie: A smaller camp liked that her manual close spared both the jumper's reserves and the team's exposure to vacuum.

2103515118818697677.wildcards: Recurring bits included Star Trek crossover jokes about Scotty beaming the team out, pitches to split the away team or splice in a hybrid plan, and a running gag over the correct spelling of O'Neill's name.

2102427955456815176.headline: The Ghost Ship narrowly outpaced The Fracture; Delivery and Heist trailed behind.

reasons.ghost: Crews called it the nearest mayday and lowest-risk stop, worth checking before moving on.
reasons.fracture: Many argued Gamma-3's twenty-three silent crew and missing debris meant the most lives were at stake.
reasons.delivery: Backers pointed to the captain's priority order and Zax's ticking deadline as reason duty came first.
reasons.heist: A smaller group wanted the artifact secured before rival factions could claim it.

2102427955456815176.wildcards: Jokes ran toward Ghostbusters callbacks and Romulan ale rumors, and several crews proposed splitting away teams across two or more contacts at once.

2103877507585913079.headline: Crew chased McKay's containment-field detour over securing the bridge first

reasons.detour: Backers argued the failing containment field couldn't wait, calling it a short detour that might reveal a survivor, or a threat worth knowing about before it got loose.
reasons.rommie: Backers favored locking down the bridge first for full sensors and ship control before wading into an unknown containment risk.

2103877507585913079.wildcards: Plenty called for splitting the team to hit both destinations at once, and several leaned on horror-movie logic about never investigating the ominous power drain.

2104239896114213067.headline: Fleet backed Rommie's override by a wide margin over retreat and gunfire.

reasons.A: Skeptics argued the unit hadn't shown real hostility and pushed for a cautious withdrawal rather than risking Rommie or wasting ammo on armor plating.
reasons.B: Most fans read the unit's pause as caution rather than aggression and wanted Rommie to attempt contact, betting a machine-to-machine link could win an ally or ship access worth more than a fight.
reasons.C: A vocal minority distrusted the override or simply wanted the P-90s to settle it fast, decisive risk be damned.

2104239896114213067.wildcards: A recurring pitch was to pair B with C as a fallback if the override failed, alongside jokes nicknaming Rommie 'Rom-doll' and worry the unit could hijack her instead.

2104602282491019492.headline: Fleet chose to seal up and cross the breach — A won big over B

reasons.A: Crews pointed to the fading containment field and ebbing power source, judged the breach the fastest route to the bridge with EV suits already on, and trusted Rommie's confidence and vacuum immunity to see them through.
reasons.B: A smaller contingent worried that venting the compartment was violent and unpredictable, and wanted to keep a sealed retreat path rather than gamble on returning to the jumper.

2104602282491019492.wildcards: Crews kept quoting "once more unto the breach" and punning on "seal up," joked about Rommie's one-armed takedown of the wrench-throwing bot, and wondered whether the disabled utility unit still held ship data worth extracting.

2104964671002251496.headline: Rommie made the leap, chosen by an overwhelming fleet consensus.

reasons.A: A minority argued O'Neill should lead as team commander, unwilling to let someone else carry the risk he was ready to take himself.
reasons.B: A handful backed Daniel mainly for variety, or on the grounds that he simply needed something to do.
reasons.C: Most of the fleet reasoned Rommie was the obvious pick since vacuum and a hard landing can't hurt an android, making her both the safest crosser and the strongest anchor for the tether.

2104964671002251496.wildcards: Several fans proposed skipping the jump entirely by mag-booting along the walls or ceiling instead, and running jokes about 'android overuse' and McKay drawing the short straw kept resurfacing.

2105327058440339834.headline: O'Neill's C4 carried the vote by a wide margin over the stroll.

reasons.A: Backers favored the spacewalk as the safer, less destructive route, even though it cost more time.
reasons.B: Backers wanted speed and trusted O'Neill's expertise, treating the C4 as both the fastest fix and the fun choice.
reasons.C: A small minority preferred retreating outright, wary that a locked, powered door meant something was guarding the far side.

2105327058440339834.wildcards: A running joke held that "when in doubt, C4" settles everything, and one fan proposed a fourth option splitting the team between the hull walk and the door.

2105689446930694283.headline: The fleet voted decisively to wake the android, 248 votes to 87.

reasons.A: Most reasoned the android was the best source of answers against whatever was skittering in the walls, and trusted Daniel and Rommie to handle first contact.
reasons.B: A cautious minority preferred gathering intelligence from the bridge first, wary of waking an unknown android before confirming it wasn't hostile.

2105689446930694283.wildcards: Replicator theories ran rampant among the crew, alongside lighter chatter about recruiting the android as ship's cook and nostalgia for classic O'Neill-Jackson banter.

2106051834058342626.headline: The fleet voted decisively to let Daniel talk Maia around, well ahead of stasis or a forced link.

reasons.A: The cautious minority preferred to put Maia straight back under, reasoning the team already had a damaged ship and an unknown risk on its hands and could sort her out later.
reasons.B: Most fans backed Daniel as the fleet's resident diplomat, arguing Maia's talk of legal action was no real threat and that honest explanation was the safest way to win her help without provoking her.
reasons.C: A small group wanted Rommie to force the link immediately, betting she could outmatch Maia outright and end the standoff before it dragged on.

2106051834058342626.wildcards: Several fans plotted fallback chains (try Daniel, then Rommie or stasis if that fails), and more than one went hunting for the in-universe Traugott Corporation's own website as a running joke.

2106414222142005299.headline: Fleet chose to allow the interface, yes topping no by nearly two to one.

reasons.yes: Most yes voters treated it as Rommie's call to make, trusting her to handle or sever the link herself if Maia proved hostile.
reasons.no: No voters distrusted an unknown android reading Rommie's memories, arguing the risk to her outweighed whatever the deal bought.

2106414222142005299.wildcards: A recurring current held that the decision wasn't the fleet's to make at all, only Rommie's, alongside jokes about backing her up first and demands that any data-sharing go both ways.

2106776610502238604.headline: Fleet overwhelmingly backed Maia's deal, 138 to 6, wary but committed.

reasons.yes: Most trusted Rommie's read on Maia and treated the deal as the fastest route to the bridge and answers about the intruder, bracing for a double-cross but moving forward anyway.
reasons.no: The holdouts balked at the word purge, arguing the crew knew too little about the entity's nature or motives to commit to destroying it.

2106776610502238604.wildcards: Side chatter ran to Replicator and Thor theories, requests for anti-replicator weapons, and jokes about Q moonlighting as Maia's lawyer.

2107138998250492164.headline: Caution won: the fleet sent Rommie to confirm the leak before trusting Maia.

reasons.C: Most crews still didn't trust Maia and wanted Rommie to verify the leak herself before anyone followed her lead.
reasons.B: A sizeable minority argued the team had already chosen to trust Maia and backing out now would be an insult with little payoff.
reasons.A: A small handful wanted to push straight through, willing to bet the warning was overcautious rather than lose time on verification.

2107138998250492164.wildcards: Plenty of jokes about not trusting the 'clanker', replicators in the walls, and the mysterious skittering noise, plus a few votes for sending a tricorder instead of risking Rommie alone.

2107501385637855667.headline: The fleet split the team decisively, leaving the other options far behind.

reasons.A: A lone vote preferred letting Rommie finish decoding the data, treating the way-home clue as worth the wait.
reasons.B: A few wanted to chase the fading life sign immediately, worried it would disappear for good if the team waited.
reasons.C: A minority argued for saving the ship first, reasoning the data and the life sign are moot if the reactor breaches.
reasons.D: Most trusted O'Neill to divide the group so the data, the life sign, and the reactor all got tackled before the clock ran out, even though no subteam stayed at full strength.

2107501385637855667.wildcards: Fans leaned hard on the "never split the party" trope and horror-movie references, debated swapping which android went with which group, and floated calling in backup from the Enterprise.

2107863773310833084.headline: Trusting Maia won decisively over running for backup and opening fire.

reasons.A: They were convinced the spiders were replicators on reflex and wanted McKay protecting the core by force.
reasons.B: They judged warning O'Neill and the team more useful than standing his ground against an unknown threat.
reasons.C: They trusted Maia's calm and her read on the ship's systems over McKay's trigger-happy instincts.

2107863773310833084.wildcards: Several fans wanted McKay to split the difference, firing while backing away or covering Maia before bolting, and more than one joked he'd only end up shooting himself or the core.

2108226161465590106.headline: Backing Maia polled 160-71, but the captain sent McKay to the hangar instead.

reasons.A: Backers said McKay's instincts would send him straight for the hangar to alert the team and start evacuating without wasting the countdown on an unproven android.
reasons.B: Most reasoned McKay wouldn't wander the wreck alone and should stick with Maia to the bridge, where Rommie already was, trading a few minutes for safety and goodwill.

2108226161465590106.wildcards: Several crew riffed on the '42 minutes' countdown as a Hitchhiker's Guide nod and joked about relief that the threat wasn't replicators, while a few proposed a hybrid: head for the bridge but radio the rest of the team along the way.

2108588549012644146.headline: Keeping Rhea hidden leads, with beaming her to safety and confronting Maia close behind.

reasons.A: Fans want Rhea beamed to sick bay fast, treating her injuries first and sorting out the android question once she's safely off the ship.
reasons.B: Voters favor bringing Maia and Rhea face to face now, betting a direct confrontation will expose whichever one is lying before more time is lost.
reasons.C: The largest bloc wants Rhea's warning kept quiet while the team regroups, calling a hidden ace the safer play until Maia's story can be checked.

2108588549012644146.wildcards: Several fans keep clocking the actor's resemblance to Stargate's Dr. Lam, and more than a few suspect Rhea or Maia could turn out to be a replicator or the entity in disguise.
